acceptanceCriteria: Specs that reference a seed directly or through a registry key get exactly those setup files.
A computed lookup, unknown key, missing path or empty spec list yields ALL with a typed reason.
A hub file that lists every seed is not followed and does not widen the result.
The output records the revision and a digest of the inputs read.
The result can be passed to the test provider so a run executes only those setup files.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1030 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem Browser suites often have setup projects that seed shared data. Running all of them before every run wastes time, and under load a seed the specs never read can fail and abort the run. Current workaround A script follows imports and string keys from the spec files to the data contexts they read, and passes the resulting setup files to the test config. It falls back to all on a computed lookup, an unknown key, or a hub file that lists every scenario. Proposal `corvint tests setup-select --specs <paths>` (and an MCP tool) returns the setup files the specs transitively depend on. It reuses the string-key registry dialect of impact analysis, returns an explicit ALL with a reason when it cannot resolve something, and binds the result to the revision. See beamfall/corvint#1030 for the full text.
title: tests: select only the setup/seed files a run needs, failing closed to all (issue #1030)
